description: A single-panel scatter plot (Figure 2) of austenite lattice parameter (nm) on the y-axis against relative alloying (wt pct) on the x-axis. The y-axis is labelled "Austenite Lattice Parameter (nm)" and spans 0.358 to 0.36 with printed ticks at 0.358, 0.359 and 0.36; the x-axis is labelled "Relative Alloying (wt pct)" and spans 0 to 3 with printed ticks at 0, 1, 2 and 3. Three labelled data points are plotted: bold "Base" at relative alloying 0, and bold "2.5 Si" and "2.5 Al", both at approximately 2.5 wt pct. The "Base" and "2.5 Si" markers sit at essentially the same height, just above the 0.358 gridline and clearly below 0.359, whereas the "2.5 Al" marker lies much higher, immediately below the 0.36 gridline. Each marker carries a small vertical error bar; no numeric coordinates are printed anywhere on the panel. The figure therefore demonstrates graphically that equal additions of Al and Si do not change the austenite lattice parameter equally: Al clearly expands the lattice while Si leaves it almost unchanged — the quantitative Δa values come from the caption and citing text, not from the pixels.

subfigures.description: Scatter plot of austenite lattice parameter (nm) vs relative alloying (wt pct) with three labelled points, Base (x = 0), 2.5 Si and 2.5 Al (both x ≈ 2.5), each with a small vertical error bar. The 2.5 Al point sits near the 0.36 gridline while Base and 2.5 Si sit just above 0.358.

observations.observation: The figure is a single scatter plot with y-axis labelled "Austenite Lattice Parameter (nm)" spanning 0.358 to 0.36 (ticks at 0.358, 0.359, 0.36) and x-axis labelled "Relative Alloying (wt pct)" spanning 0 to 3 (ticks at 0, 1, 2, 3).
Three data points are labelled in bold on the plot: "Base" at relative alloying 0, and "2.5 Si" and "2.5 Al" both at approximately 2.5 wt pct on the x-axis.

The "2.5 Al" point lies highest in the plot, immediately below the 0.36 gridline, whereas the "Base" and "2.5 Si" points lie at essentially the same height, just above the 0.358 gridline and below 0.359.
Each of the three markers carries a small vertical error bar, and no numeric data labels are printed next to the points.
The caption states the figure shows the dependence of austenite lattice parameter on Si and Al alloying.
The citing text states that 2.5 wt.% Al increases the austenite lattice parameter by 1.41 × 10⁻³ nm relative to the base alloy.
The citing text states that 2.5 wt.% Si has a minimal effect on the austenite lattice parameter.

The citing text states that relative Si alloying is the difference in Si content between the 2.5 Si and base alloys, and relative Al alloying the difference in Al content between the two alloys, all other elements being approximately equal.
The citing text reports calculated linear lattice parameter coefficients A^LP for Si and Al of 0.018 and 0.582 × 10⁻³ nm wt.%⁻¹, respectively, stated to agree well with Dyson and Holmes (Table 2).

measured_quantities: change in austenite lattice parameter (10⁻³ nm)
linear lattice parameter coefficient A^LP (10⁻³ nm wt.%⁻¹)
unreadable_items: Exact marker coordinates are not printed on the panel; y-values of the three points can only be read against the ticks (Base and 2.5 Si fall between 0.358 and 0.359; 2.5 Al falls just below 0.36).
Error-bar magnitudes are not quantified or labelled.
